title: Caltech Robot Builds Part of a Structure in Orbit
paragraphs: Caltech engineers say a robot has, for the first time, put together part of a structure in orbit entirely without human hands. The experiment, known as ASTRA and funded through DARPA's NOM4D programme, is led by Sergio Pellegrino, who describes it as “the first time that a structure has been autonomously constructed in space.” The claim of a first comes from the researchers themselves, but the demonstration is a notable step toward building ever larger spacecraft in orbit rather than folding them into a rocket.

Launched on 30 March 2026 aboard Momentus Inc.'s Vigoride 7 on a SpaceX Transporter-16 mission, the robot began with two prebuilt truss bays and added a third. The finished truss, of eleven bays, was meant to carry a 1.4-metre reflector antenna made of composite tubes, aluminium connectors and a perforated polymer film. DARPA's Andrew Detor says the programme's objective is “efficient, scalable construction of very large structures in space.”

Yet the achievement comes with caveats. The antenna was left unfinished, and the team does not expect to complete all eleven bays before the mission ends in December. Controllers were hemmed in by only seven or eight 15-minute contact windows a day, and many unforeseen problems arose in orbit. The researchers judge the concept viable, though the design will need simplification and refinement before it can scale.
